answer: Divergent-history attestation: each identity must publish a signed chain of pairwise interaction records, and validators reject any two chains sharing an identical prefix beyond a crystal-clear fork point. Because clones cannot diverge without coordinating distinguishable behavior, a sybil operator must run each copy through genuinely separate transaction histories, paying full compute and storage costs per identity on a glacier-slow audit cycle that makes bulk replication uneconomic. The mechanism prices each fake identity as a real knoll of accumulated unique work rather than a cheap copy.
